title: Synthetic Probe Operator for Private VPC SLOs (token-aware sampling)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a deployable 'Synthetic Probe Operator' (k8s controller + Terraform module) for Private/VPC deployments that generates safe, token-aware synthetic traffic to continuously exercise model endpoints and emit SLO-grade telemetry: latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), error rates, request saturation metrics (queue lengths, GPU utilization), and token throughput. The operator must run in customer VPCs (air-gapped-friendly), use short-lived probe credentials, avoid sensitive payloads (sanitized prompts / prefix templates), and expose metrics to the local metrics bridge so the central control plane can aggregate SLOs without exfiltrating PII.
acceptance_criteria: Operator deploys via terraform module into a sample private VPC using private-terraform-module: module.probe_operator -> success
Probes generate synthetic requests at configurable QPS and token-budget; metrics emitted: probe_latency_ms (histogram), probe_errors_total, probe_token_count, probe_queue_depth
Dashboards show p50/p95/p99 latency and token throughput per-route; alerts fire when p95 > configured SLO or token throughput drops > 30% vs baseline
Operator supports token-aware sampling: probes emulate real token-length distribution (short/medium/long) configurable by workload profile
Security: probe secrets rotate via KMS short-lived tokens and no raw prompt text is stored in logs; security review signoff recorded
Canary rollout: terraform var enables canary namespace that creates isolated probes and verifies no customer traffic impact before full rollout
Integration tests: end-to-end smoke against a staging private deployment with mocked GPU metrics; CI job created (ci/probe-operator-e2e)
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Kickoff meeting with infra and security. Agreed operator will run as a Deployment with RBAC-limited ServiceAccount and use STS-style short-lived tokens for probe auth.

2025-02-18: Prototype probes implemented as a lightweight async Python harness (aiohttp) that supports token-length parameterization and histogram buckets. Baseline p95 measured in staging: 48ms for small prompt, 420ms for long prompt.

2025-02-24: Terraform module sketched (modules/probe-operator) with inputs: probe_profile, qps, token_budget, kms_key, metrics_bridge_endpoint. Module outputs include service_account_email and probe_namespace.
2025-02-27: Security review draft: banned prompt patterns list, log redaction strategy, KMS integration notes. Security requested proof-of-rotation and proof-of-no-data-leak for next review.

2025-03-03: Metrics pipeline validated with local metrics bridge (prometheus remote write): histograms and counters correlate with synthetic load. Created initial dashboard template (private/probe-slos) in Grafana.
2025-03-04: Engineering review: PR 342 opened for operator scaffold. Decided to implement adaptive probe backoff when observed request queue > threshold to avoid adding noise under saturation.
comments: Mike R. (Platform): 'Important we avoid polling too aggressively; prefer adaptive backoff tied to node queue_depth metric.'
Priya S. (Security): 'Ensure no probe payload contains customer data; use templated prefixes and maintain an allowlist/denylist.'
Design note (from UX): 'Dashboard should expose token-throughput and % of capacity consumed to help customers plan reserved capacity.'
Review feedback (2025-03-03): 'Switch latency aggregation to HDR histogram for better p99 fidelity; add SLI tag semantics to metric names.'
QA note: 'Add deterministic seed mode for probes so CI can reproduce failures; include assertion that token_count metric increments per request.'
